### Florida State University I study political violence and its consequences for individuals, institutions, and post-conflict societies. My research lies at the intersection of comparative politics and international security, with particular interests in conflict-related sexual violence, political behavior, peacebuilding, and gender and conflict.
[Research](research.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Curriculum Vitae](cv.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary} [Email](mailto:rsmarriott@fsu.edu){.btn .btn-outline-primary} [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0009-0001-6405-3123){.btn .btn-outline-primary} [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rachel-marriott){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
![](headshot.jpeg){fig-alt="Rachel Marriott"}
--- ## About I am a Ph.D. student in Political Science at Florida State University. My research examines how violence shapes political behavior, institutional responses, and post-conflict political development. I am particularly interested in understanding how violence transforms political institutions, shapes public attitudes, and influences long-term political development. My current work focuses on conflict-related sexual violence, survivor behavior, women's participation in peace processes, and the design of post-conflict institutions. More broadly, I am interested in political violence, comparative political behavior, peacebuilding, democratic institutions, and gender and conflict. Before beginning my Ph.D. at FSU, I earned a B.S. in Political Science and French, *summa cum laude*, from the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), where I also competed as an NCAA women's soccer student-athlete. --- ## Research Interests

Comparative Politics · International Relations · Political Violence · International Security · Political Behavior · Women, Peace and Security · Peacebuilding

--- ## Research My research is organized around three broad themes: **Political Violence and Conflict.**\ I study how exposure to violence affects individuals, communities, and political institutions, with particular attention to conflict-related sexual violence and post-conflict political behavior. **Gender and Peacebuilding.**\ I examine women's participation in peace processes, gender provisions in peace agreements, and the ways conflict-related harms shape institutional design and post-conflict politics. **Political Behavior and Institutions.**\ My broader research considers how institutions, social environments, and experiences of violence shape political attitudes, participation, and democratic development. --- ## Current Projects **Survivor Behavior After Conflict-Related Sexual Violence**\ This project examines how survivors make decisions about disclosure, reporting, and help-seeking following conflict-related sexual violence, with particular attention to stigma, trust, and institutional context. **From Atrocity to Agreement: Wartime Sexual Violence in Peace Agreement Design**\ This project investigates whether higher levels of wartime sexual violence are associated with the inclusion of gender provisions in comprehensive peace agreements. **Women's Participation and Peace Agreement Design**\ This research examines how women's formal participation in peace negotiations and women's civil society participation shape the inclusion of gender provisions in peace agreements. --- ## Additional Information For more information about my research, publications, conference presentations, and teaching, please see my [Research](research.qmd) page or [Curriculum Vitae](cv.qmd).
